text:
IncidentBot: 🚨 Alert: elevated 5xx rate for model 'redwood-translate:v3' in region prod-eu. Error spike started ~10:12 UTC. Paging on-call @Emma.
Emma: I'm on it. seeing ~18% 5xx on the v3 traffic slice in cloud-prod-eu. Can someone grab metrics & any recent deploys? @Liam @Sanjay
Liam: I rolled a small config change to the kernel selection last night but nothing touching v3 traffic routing. grabbing logs now.
Sanjay: infra: I see increased latency leading to downstream timeouts from the v3 shard pool. KV-cache misses are up. Could be a kernel/quantization regression. Suggest immediate mitigation: stop new requests to v3 and steer traffic to v2. fast rollback path is safer than debugging live.
Emma: Agreed. Plan: 1) set v3 weight to 0 (drain), 2) promote v2 as default, 3) apply temporary rate limits for heavy customers. Anyone object? :+1: or :thumbsdown:
Maria: Support update: we've got 3 P1 customer reports and ~22 tickets for degraded translations. Sales alerted. We'll post a short PS update after mitigation.
Liam: I'll do the traffic cut. Using rcli to avoid console latency. Command:
```
# drain v3 in prod-eu
rcli traffic set --model redwood-translate --variant v3 --region prod-eu --weight 0 --auth-token $RC_TOKEN
# ensure v2 is default
rcli release promote --model redwood-translate --variant v2 --region prod-eu --auth-token $RC_TOKEN
```
Emma: Also add quick per-customer quotas for the top 5 tenants to protect tails. Example:
```
rcli quotas update --customer big-retailer --model redwood-translate --region prod-eu --qps 5
rcli quotas update --customer acme-corp --model redwood-translate --region prod-eu --qps 3
```
Sanjay: I'll watch the autoscaler and shard health. If any shard still answers with v3, we'll kill the pool and bounce. Also enabling verbose logs on v3 for forensic data (no rollback yet) so we can capture stack traces.
DeployBot: Action executed: traffic update accepted for model redwood-translate in prod-eu. v3 weight -> 0. Request id: req-0ab3f7
DeployBot: Action executed: release promote accepted. default variant -> v2. Request id: req-0ab3f8
Liam: Confirmed by metrics: within 30s of the traffic change we see 5xx drop from 18% -> 1.2% for translate requests in prod-eu. Latency normalized for most tenants.
Maria: Support: initial customer triage: 2 customers saw degraded translations for ~8 minutes, both auto-recovered after traffic shift. Opening follow-up case notes for RU-asap.
Emma: Handoff: I'm going to take a short break, passing on on-call to @Jules for next 30 mins while I coordinate postmortem notes.
Jules: oncall ack. Monitoring graphs look stable. Keeping an eye on v3 logs collection (S3 path: s3://redwood-incidents/1789456123-v3-dumps).
Sanjay: Next steps for incident: 1) collect v3 crash logs & cache metrics, 2) reproduce v3 failure on staging with same kernel/quantization flags, 3) set evaluation job to compare outputs v2 vs v3, 4) run a controlled canary once fixed.
Emma: I'll file the incident ticket (inc-2026-1789456123) and add postmortem leads: Liam + Sanjay + Maria. Maria will draft customer communication.
Maria: Draft PS to be reviewed: "We observed an elevated error rate for translations served by variant v3 in EU. Traffic was rolled back to v2 within 10 minutes; most customers recovered automatically. Investigations are ongoing and we will follow up with root cause and timeline." Will share in #product for signoff.
Liam: Quick note - we should consider a temporary block on auto-deploys to v3 until we run a canary harness with the new kernel change. I'll open a PR for a gating check.
IncidentBot: Incident inc-2026-1789456123: mitigation in place (traffic rolled back). Status: monitoring. Severity: degraded. Escalation: none. Next update in 30m or on significant change.
Emma: Thanks team. Great quick work. :clap: Closing active mitigation but ticket stays open for investigations and follow-up tasks.
Jules: Will keep watch and ping if anything creeps up."
